newsitem.title: UK: Glaxo, drug shares off after ADR weakness.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo, drug shares off after ADR weakness.

text.p: Glaxo Wellcome Plc and other leading UK drug stocks dipped in early trade on Tuesday, echoing losses in their ADRS in the U.S. as a report in the Financial Times questioned whether the sector's gains would continue.

Glaxo was down 13-1/2p at 13.32 stg by 0727, after its ADRs fell $14/16 to $43-7/16. SmithKline Beecham Plc, whose ADRs fell $1-11/16 to $100-7/16, dropped 10p to 12.30 stg and Zeneca Group Plc, down $1-7/8 in New York, lost 10-1/2p to 2030 stg.
"The whole drug sector was weaker in New York," said one dealer.

Meanwhile the FT said recent gains in drug stocks could continue although the sentiment towards the sector could sour. It said the greater liquidity in drug shares could be vulnerable to a sell-off if the whole market turned down, adding that sales growth could suffer if plans were revived to reform the U.S. healthcare sector.
Separately, Lehman Brothers repeated a "neutral" rating on Glaxo ahead of its results on Thursday.

Analyst Jo Walton at the investment bank said Glaxo may find it tough to reach its target of double-digit earnings growth because of its exposure to slower-growing areas such as anti-infectives and inhaled steroids.
